name: OWASP Top 10 Application Security Risks (2021)
description: Compliance rules aligned with the OWASP Top 10 (2021) standard categories.

rules.title: SQL Injection
rules.summary: User-supplied data is not sanitized, filtered, or parameterized by the application before query construction.
rules.description: SQL Injection occurs when untrusted input is interpreted as SQL commands.

rules.title: OS Command Injection
rules.summary: Application executes system commands containing concatenated user data.
rules.description: Command Injection allows remote arbitrary command execution.

rules.title: LDAP Injection
rules.summary: Application constructs LDAP search filters using unvalidated input.
rules.description: LDAP injection allows unauthorized directory querying or authentication bypass.

rules.title: XPath Injection
rules.summary: Application evaluates dynamic XPath queries constructed with untrusted input.
rules.description: XPath injection allows unauthorized XML document querying.

rules.title: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read
rules.summary: Application allows users to manipulate file paths to access files outside the intended directory.
rules.description: Path traversal leads to arbitrary file access or information disclosure.

rules.title: Weak or Deprecated Cryptographic Ciphers
rules.summary: Use of broken or obsolete cryptographic algorithms such as DES, RC4, or AES-ECB mode.
rules.description: Cryptographic failures compromise data confidentiality and integrity.

rules.title: Broken Hash Algorithms (MD5 / SHA-1)
rules.summary: Use of collision-prone hash algorithms for integrity or cryptographic protection.
rules.description: MD5 and SHA-1 have known collision vulnerabilities and should be replaced with SHA-256.

rules.title: Predictable Pseudorandom Number Generation
rules.summary: Use of predictable PRNGs for security-sensitive tokens, passwords, or salts.
rules.description: Use SecureRandom instead of Random or Math.random() for security tokens.
